x_failures: Attributes to Dyscolus p.184 that beans 'buried in the ground and later dug up... would appear like a human child', and that they contain 'the same substance as human heads'. The page only says that a boiled bean exposed to the moon produces blood. The image caption calls Rivinus p.267 'Faba minor (the broad bean)', but that page shows a white lupine.
reason: All of Y's quotations appear on the cited pages: the Hierocles quote on p.181, Beroaldo's 'abstain from the Republic', Taylor on p.12 and the linen note on p.71. Some of Y's material is loosely relevant, but X misstates what Dyscolus p.184 says and mislabels a lupine plate as a bean.
